text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — ran a hybrid sweep on the A100 pool (8x A100 80GB, NCCL 2.14) to test channel count + algo/proto combos with LL and LL128. Found a regression when combining LL128 + 4 channels + proto=ring for medium-length sequences (seq=1024). Throughput drops ~18% vs baseline (LL + 2 channels + proto=tree). KV-cache hit rate also dipped ~3ppt which is suspicious. Logs + perf attached below.

emily: ugh, interesting. do you have the perf traces? especially overlap traces for allreduce vs matmul.

sanjay: pasted a short summary: tokens/sec (avg across 16 concurrent streams): baseline 76k t/s, LL128+4ch+ring 62k t/s. p99 latency baseline 245ms -> 312ms. allreduce tail jumps from 4.8ms -> 12.6ms on some ranks. KV-cache hit from 87% -> 84%.
kai: can you share the NCCL envs you used? ordering, channel map, comm APIs?
sanjay: sure — config snippet: ```export NCCL_ALGO=ring
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
export NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=4
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0
# runtime: tensor+pipeline mixed with 2-way tp
```
adrian: two quick things: 1) LL128 with 4 channels can increase small-message concurrencies but may balloon rendezvous overhead for medium chunk sizes. 2) proto=ring may cause different ordering of collectives that interacts badly with our chunking in the KV cache prefetch path.
emily: do we know which ranks see the big allreduce? is it symmetric? or a subset?
sanjay: it's asymmetric. ranks 2 and 5 show 3x higher allreduce times. traced callstacks point to NVLink contention during the reduce-scatter phase. i attached a flame-style summary from our perf tracer: "reduce_scatter" hotspots aligned with cudaMemcpyAsync bursts.

kai: could be channel-to-GPU mapping imbalance. we changed channel affinity recently to try to avoid link oversubscription. maybe that mapping + ring proto causes some ranks to route across different NVLink paths.
adrian: suggestion: try proto=tree with LL128 + 4ch and compare. Also run with NCCL_CHECK_DISABLE=1? (jk) — but enable NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1? Not sure. Another knob: NCCL_ALGO=ring vs tree vs tree:0 etc.
sanjay: ran two quick experiments: (A) LL128 + 4ch + proto=tree -> tokens/sec 74k (close to baseline). (B) LL + 4ch + proto=ring -> 71k. So proto choice seems to matter a lot with LL128.
emily: so LL128 itself isn't the culprit, it's the coupling with proto=ring. odd. maybe ring's scatter pattern interacts with our KV-prefetch chunk size. what's kv chunk size?
sanjay: default prefetch chunk is 256 tokens per shard. When we increased prefetch chunk to 512, the hit-rate decreased more under the bad combo. Suspect that larger prefetch causes extra simultaneous injections of medium-size NCCL messages that amplify link contention.
kai: can you drop channel count to 2 with LL128+ring? that might reduce concurrency and restore perf.
sanjay: did that: LL128 + 2ch + ring -> 73.5k t/s, p99 255ms. allreduce tail back to ~5.2ms. KV hit ~86.5%.
adrian: ok that strongly points to channel-level parallelism causing imbalanced micro-queueing on some NVLinks when proto=ring. For now, plan: document safe defaults per model/sequence length and add an automated guard in the runtime to prefer 2 channels for seq>512 when proto=ring + LL128. Also add a check during rollout to run a short overlap micro-benchmark.
emily: agree. add an experiment to see if mapping channels to physical links differently fixes it. we can try NCCL_MAX_NRINGS or NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL?
kai: another data point: on V100 cluster (older interconnect), the combo didn't regress — suggests it's NVLink topology dependent. Good to add per-hardware profile.
sanjay: filed a quick ticket: INF-3321 with traces. I'll push a prototype guard into runtime: when (proto==ring && proto_impl==LL128 && seq>512) { max_channels = 2 } and run regression test.
adrian: also add telemetry: report effective channel count, proto, avg allreduce time per rank to console so we can detect in prod.
emily: perf-bot, can you run the standard microbench with synthetic workload (seq=1024, bs=1, 16 streams) across the canary A100 pool with channel counts 1..6 and both proto=ring/tree and LL vs LL128?
perf-bot: Scheduling microbench run INF-MICRO-907, target pool: canary-a100-8. Will run ring/tree x LL/LL128 x channels=1..6, 3 runs each. ETA ~45m. Results will be posted here. :robot_face:

sanjay: thanks — after perf-bot posts results we can codify the guard and a per-hardware recommendation table. Also we should add a small change to KV cache prefetch policy: if channels>2 and proto=ring and seq>512, throttle prefetch concurrency.
kai: can you also capture per-link utilization (nvidia-smi topo stats / nvlink counters) during the run? that would help correlate.
sanjay: yes will capture NVLink counters + nsight traces for the worst run.
emily: awesome. TL;DR: regression caused by interaction of LL128+ring+high-channel-count on A100 NVLink topology -> leads to asymmetric allreduce tail + worse kv prefetch behavior. Mitigation: reduce channels to 2 for this combo, throttle prefetch, add telemetry, per-hardware profile.
adrian: filing follow-ups: - INF-3322 run mapping experiments - INF-3323 add runtime guard + telemetry - INF-3324 KV prefetch backpressure.
sanjay: thanks all. will update INF-3321 with links to traces and perf-bot output when available. :rocket:
